chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Ishaq Shaeer, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about pre-emption (shuf'ah) in houses: Is it an obligatory right for the partner, and is it presented to the neighbor so that he is more entitled to it than others? He said: Pre-emption in sales applies when there is a partner, so he is more entitled to it with the price.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on pre-emption (shuf'ah) for partners versus neighbors in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the foundational Shia jurisprudence on pre-emption (shuf'ah), prioritizing the co-owner's right to acquire a sold share over that of a neighbor. It reflects the early juristic consensus that the primary purpose of shuf'ah is to prevent unwanted co-ownership, thereby preserving the integrity of existing partnerships in property. This ruling underscores the practical application of justice in commercial transactions within the Shia legal tradition.
